subject: planets
title: The 5 Coldest Planets, Ranked (#1 Barely Beats #2)

scenes.text: The coldest planet is a billion miles past number two, and only five degrees colder.
Number five: Mars. Minus 65 Celsius on average, colder than Antarctica.
scenes.label: Mars · -65 °C

scenes.text: Number four: Jupiter. Minus 110, even though it makes some of its own heat.
scenes.label: Jupiter · -110 °C

scenes.text: Number three: Saturn. Minus 140, at the cloud layer where pressure matches Earth's air.
scenes.label: Saturn · -140 °C

scenes.text: Number two: Uranus. Minus 195, a planet tipped on its side.
scenes.label: Uranus · -195 °C

scenes.text: Number one: Neptune. Minus 200. A billion miles farther out, and just five degrees colder.
scenes.label: Neptune · -200 °C

description:
Mean temperatures from NASA's planetary fact sheet: Mars -65 °C, Jupiter -110 °C, Saturn -140 °C, Uranus -195 °C and Neptune -200 °C (for the giant planets, measured where the pressure equals sea level on Earth).
Neptune orbits about 30 times Earth's distance from the Sun, Uranus about 19, yet they differ by only five degrees.
Why do you think Neptune isn't much colder?
first_comment: Which would you put at #1 if moons counted too? And what should we rank next?
